findings.evidence: Candidate (07 ¶21): "including an electric motor driving an eccentric mass, a pneumatic vibrator, and a linear oscillator. In the embodiment of FIG. 1 the vibration motor 18 is a housing standing directly on the base 12, wider along the long edge of the base 12 than it is tall." Nearest source (disclosure ¶11): "a vibration motor coupled to a first side of a rigid base."
findings.fix: In 07 ¶21 replace the first two sentences with "The vibration motor 18 may be of any type that produces mechanical vibration in the base 12." In figures/FIG-1 reduce the motor bullet to "The vibration motor 18 is a rectangular housing standing on the top face of the slab at its left end, its front face one large blank rectangle with no body in front of it. Identified well inside that face."

findings.title: Air-extraction alternatives (fan, blower, ejector) and the self-contained/no-hose assertion are untraced
findings.detail: The disclosure gives one example only — 'such as a vacuum pump'. The candidate adds a fan, a blower and an ejector supplied with compressed air as alternative mechanisms, and asserts that the pump is carried on the base so that the device is self-contained with no hose running back to a separate machine. None of these appears in any affirmative USER passage.
findings.evidence: Candidate (07 ¶25): "Other air-extraction mechanisms 20 that withdraw air from the chamber 22 may be used, including a fan or blower, or an ejector supplied with compressed air." and "so that the vibration device 10 is self-contained and no hose runs back to a separate machine." Nearest source (disclosure ¶11): "An air-extraction mechanism, such as a vacuum pump, is also coupled to the first side..."
findings.fix: In 07 ¶25 delete the sentence beginning "Other air-extraction mechanisms 20..." and delete "so that the vibration device 10 is self-contained and no hose runs back to a separate machine", leaving "In the embodiment shown, the air-extraction mechanism 20 is a vacuum pump carried on the base 12."

findings.title: Bearing-face width design rule and flush/proud facing variants are untraced
findings.detail: The candidate teaches that the width of the bearing face simultaneously sets the contact pressure and the length and flow resistance of the leakage path, and that a wider face spreads contact and lengthens the path while a narrower one concentrates and shortens it; it also offers the facing flush with or standing proud of one or both sides of the perimeter member. The disclosure contains no dimension, no contact-pressure teaching, no flow-path-length teaching and no flush/proud variant. The drafting agent's turn records 'perimeter and base dimensions' as a point where the disclosure gives no fact.
findings.evidence: Candidate (07 ¶37): "The low-friction facing 28 may be flush with the outer and inner sides of the perimeter member 24, or it may stand a little proud of one or both of them... it sets the contact pressure at which the holding force is delivered into the exposed face 38, and, because the clearance 34 described below runs beneath that width, it sets the length of the flow path..." Nearest source (disclosure ¶13): "Instead, it restricts airflow into the chamber while maintaining rigid contact with the tile."
findings.fix: Delete 07 ¶37 in full.

findings.title: Self-restoring holding force narrative, chip, trapped grain and lippage step are untraced
findings.detail: The candidate asserts a comparative failure mode for sealed devices and a self-restoring characteristic for this one, invoking a chip in the exposed face, a grain of bonding material caught under the perimeter, tilting past a lippage step between two covering elements, and a device that 'does not have a state of being attached at all'. The disclosure contrasts the invention with suction cups on the grounds of damping and fixed attachment only; it never describes seal breach, dropping, lippage or self-restoration.
findings.evidence: Candidate (07 ¶57): "any breach of the seal, such as a chip in the exposed face 38, a grain of bonding material 40 caught under the perimeter, or a moment of tilting as the device passes a lippage step between two covering elements 36, releases the vacuum and drops the device." Nearest source (disclosure ¶7): "A conventional suction cup also attaches the machine at one fixed location, preventing it from sliding across the tile and causing vibration intensity to decrease at areas farther from the attachment point."
findings.fix: Delete 07 ¶57 in full; amend ¶55 to "A property of this arrangement should be noted, because it is what the arrangement is for."; and change the opening of ¶59 from "Second, and for the same reason, the" to "The".

findings.title: Covering element and substrate enumerations are untraced
findings.detail: The candidate enumerates the covering element as a ceramic or porcelain tile, a stone slab, a large-format panel, and the substrate as a floor screed, a wall, a backer board. The disclosure says 'tiles and other covering materials' and 'the underlying substrate' only; none of the enumerated species appears in any affirmative USER passage, and 'a wall' additionally imports the unsupported vertical-surface use.
findings.evidence: Candidate (07 ¶7): "A covering element 36, which may be a ceramic or porcelain tile, a stone slab, a large-format panel or a similar rigid covering element..." and "The substrate 42 may be a floor screed, a wall, a backer board or any other surface being covered." Nearest source (disclosure ¶5): "a vibration device for setting tiles and other covering materials into thinset, mortar, adhesive, or similar bonding material."
findings.fix: In 07 ¶7 replace the first enumeration with "A covering element 36, which may be a tile or other covering material," and replace the substrate sentence with "The substrate 42 is the surface being covered." In 03-field.md replace "tiles, slabs, panels and other covering elements" with "tiles and other covering elements".

findings.title: Claim 15 limitation that the pulling force acts substantially in the plane of the exposed face is untraced
findings.detail: The system claim requires the pulling element to be 'arranged to apply... a pulling force substantially in a plane of the exposed face'. In the description this arrangement is produced solely by the low attachment formation, which is itself untraced; strip that and the limitation has no written-description basis. The disclosure states only that pulling the flexible element moves the device across the tile.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 15): "the flexible pulling element being incapable of transmitting compression to the vibration device and being arranged to apply to the vibration device a pulling force substantially in a plane of the exposed face". (07 ¶81): "Because the attachment formation 48 is placed low, as described below, the line along which the tension acts lies close to the plane of the exposed face 38." Nearest source (disclosure ¶17): "Pulling the flexible element moves the device across the tile, while the pressure differential independently supplies the force holding the device against the surface."
findings.fix: Amend the clause in claim 15 to "a flexible pulling element connected to the vibration device, the flexible pulling element being incapable of transmitting compression to the vibration device and being arranged to move the vibration device across the exposed face when tension is applied to it,". In 07 ¶81 delete "Because the attachment formation 48 is placed low, as described below, the line along which the tension acts lies close to the plane of the exposed face 38." and amend the following sentence to "The flexible pulling element 46 is thus incapable of transmitting compression to the vibration device 10, and moves it across the exposed face 38 when tension is applied."

findings.title: Operator standing away and large working distance are untraced
findings.detail: The candidate adds an ergonomic result — the operator may stand away from the device and at a large working distance need not bend over it. The disclosure's stated results of the pulling embodiment are decoupled control, minimal pulling force, and reduced vibration, pressure, fatigue and joint stress; it says nothing about operator stance, distance or bending.
findings.evidence: Candidate (07 ¶81): "The operator may stand away from the vibration device 10, and at a large working distance need not bend over it at all." Nearest source (disclosure ¶17): "This provides decoupled control in which the operator controls position using minimal pulling force while the vacuum maintains consistent coupling and vibration transfer."
findings.fix: Delete the final sentence of 07 ¶81.

findings.title: Method steps of spreading bonding material and laying the covering element are untraced
findings.detail: The candidate claims and describes preliminary method steps of spreading the bonding material on a substrate and laying the covering element on it. The disclosure describes a device applied to a tile that has been set into bonding material; it never recites the acts of spreading or laying as steps of the invention, and no affirmative USER passage supplies them.

findings.fix: Delete claim 25 and renumber. findings.title: Background prior-art characterizations trace to no inventor source and carry unresolved [REF:...] tokens
findings.detail: Five prior-art documents are characterized in structural detail and editorialized about ('Holding and moving are alternative states of that apparatus'). Nothing in the disclosure or in any affirmative USER passage identifies these documents or their contents; the inventor's background names only 'conventional tile vibrators' generically. findings.evidence: Candidate (04 ¶9): "An example of the vibrating suction-cup approach applied to tiling is described in [REF:DE-202021002652-U1], which discloses a device provided with a handle for lifting and laying slabs..." and (04 ¶13): "Holding and moving are alternative states of that apparatus, which holds when it is not sliding and slides when it is not holding". If the attorney elects to retain prior-art discussion, move it to an Information Disclosure Statement and replace each [REF:...] token with a conventional citation (e.g. "DE 20 2021 002 652 U1").

findings.title: FIG. 1 requires the pump to touch the base nowhere, contradicting "coupled to the first side"
findings.where: figures/FIG-1 brief (air-extraction mechanism bullet); draft/08-claims.md claim 1; draft/05-summary.md ¶3; draft/07-detailed-description.md ¶9

findings.title: Detailed description says FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 show bonding material 40 and substrate 42, which neither brief depicts

The margin between the outermost and middle rectangles is by contrast a narrow border, plainly narrower than the band everywhere." findings.title: Claim count exceeds the fee-free allowance
findings.detail: The set contains 26 claims with three independents (1, 15, 20). The fee-free allowance is 20 total and 3 independent, so 6 excess claims would be charged at filing. This is a fee decision for the signing attorney, not a defect, but it should be settled before filing. The deletions recommended above (claims 4, 8, 10, 11, 12, 19, 24, 25) would bring the set to 18 claims with 3 independents, within the allowance.

findings.fix: Apply the claim deletions identified above and renumber sequentially; verify every dependency reference after renumbering (no independent claim is deleted, so claims depending on 1, 15 and 20 keep their bases). No excess-claims fee is then due.

data.summary: The candidate is a coherent, well-written application, but its source ledger does not close. The only affirmative inventor authority is disclosure.md (repeated verbatim as the first USER turn in conversation.md); every later USER turn is a resume/repair/gate instruction, and the final two are expressly corrective ("This is a source-fidelity QA repair, not additional inventor disclosure... Do not use this corrective message as source support"). That corrective turn enumerates features "already found unsupported" — a separate PTFE facing, a through-base extraction opening and duct, a support column, direct motor fasteners, exhaust to atmosphere, a no-valve limitation, cord/battery alternatives, an integral one-piece loop, an attachment formation with low placement, plural chambers and dividing walls, vertical-surface use, and bail-handle geometry — and essentially all of them are still in the claims, detailed description, numeral table, and figure briefs. Numerals 28 (low-friction facing), 30 (extraction opening), 32 (duct), 48 (attachment formation), 50 (electrical supply) and 54 (fastener) name six parts the inventor never described, and they are carried into claims 4, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14 and 19 and onto FIG. 1 through FIG. 5. Beyond that list, the description invents a base material/section teaching, a motor-type list, air-extraction alternatives (fan, blower, ejector), a bearing-face width design rule, a quantitative pump-selection rule that is claimed in claim 8, a self-restoring/lippage narrative, a treatment end point, and covering-element/substrate enumerations. I also found four internal-consistency defects: FIG. 1 requires the pump to touch the base nowhere while claim 1 and the summary recite it "coupled to the first side"; the detailed description says FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 show the covering element bedded in bonding material 40 over substrate 42, which neither brief depicts; "fasteners" names both numbered part 54 and a second unnumbered set fixing the perimeter member; and the background carries unresolved [REF:...] tokens with prior-art characterizations that trace to no inventor passage. 30 findings follow, each with a filing-clean fix.

findings.title: Separate low-friction facing 28 fixed to the perimeter member end is untraced
findings.where: draft/08-claims.md claim 4; draft/07-detailed-description.md ¶35, ¶37, ¶63; draft/06-drawings.md FIG. 4; draft/numerals.md entry 28; figures/FIG-4 brief
findings.detail: The candidate introduces a discrete two-part perimeter: a metal loop plus a PTFE facing bonded or mechanically fixed to its end, whose exposed surface forms the bearing face. The disclosure describes a one-material perimeter, not a carrier plus a separate facing, and never mentions bonding or mechanically fixing a facing. No affirmative USER passage describes a facing as a separate member. The corrective USER turn names 'a separate PTFE facing fixed to a perimeter end' as an example already found unsupported, which is not support.
findings.evidence: Candidate (07 ¶35): "the perimeter member 24 is a metal loop carrying a low-friction facing 28 of PTFE bonded or mechanically fixed to its end, and the exposed surface of the low-friction facing 28 forms the bearing face 26". Claim 4: "wherein the perimeter member comprises a low-friction facing of polytetrafluoroethylene fixed to an end of the perimeter member remote from the base". Nearest source (disclosure ¶11): "The perimeter of the second side is formed as a rigid loop or skirt made from a low-friction material such as plastic, metal, PTFE, or a combination of rigid materials." — the loop is made from the material; no separate facing is disclosed.
findings.fix: Delete claim 4 and renumber claims 5-14 accordingly. In 07 ¶35 delete the sentence beginning "In the embodiment of FIG. 4, the perimeter member 24 is a metal loop carrying a low-friction facing 28..." and retain only "the perimeter member 24 is made of a low-friction rigid material and the bearing face 26 is the end face of that member." In ¶63 replace "the base 12, the perimeter member 24 and the low-friction facing 28 forming the bearing face 26" with "the base 12 and the perimeter member 24 terminating in the bearing face 26". Delete ¶37 in full. Remove numeral 28 from draft/numerals.md, from figures/FIG-4 (identify 24 on the whole column and 26 on its bottom line, deleting the dividing boundary line), and from 06-drawings FIG. 4, which should read "...showing the bearing face at the lower end of the perimeter member, the clearance...".

findings.title: Extraction opening 30 through the base and duct 32 are untraced
findings.where: draft/08-claims.md claim 10; draft/07-detailed-description.md ¶15, ¶25, ¶45, ¶87, ¶89; draft/06-drawings.md FIG. 3; draft/numerals.md entries 30, 32; figures/FIG-1, FIG-2, FIG-3 briefs
findings.detail: The candidate specifies a hole passing through the base from the second side to the first side, a duct connecting it to the pump, and an upright hollow column open at both ends that stands on the first side and carries the pump on its upper end. The disclosure states only that the air-extraction mechanism is coupled to the first side and is in fluid communication with the chamber; it prescribes no path, no through-base opening, no duct and no column. No affirmative USER passage describes any of these. The corrective turn lists 'a through-base extraction opening, duct, support column' as already found unsupported.
findings.evidence: Candidate (07 ¶15): "An extraction opening 30 passes through the base 12 from the second side 16 to the first side 14 and places the chamber 22 in fluid communication with the air-extraction mechanism 20 through a duct 32." (07 ¶25): "The duct 32 is an upright hollow column open at both ends that stands on the first side 14 over the extraction opening 30 and carries the air-extraction mechanism 20 on its upper end". Claim 10: "further comprising an extraction opening passing through the base from the second side to the first side, and a duct connecting the extraction opening to the air-extraction mechanism." Nearest source (disclosure ¶11): "An air-extraction mechanism, such as a vacuum pump, is also coupled to the first side and is in fluid communication with a chamber located on a second side of the base." — the fact of fluid communication only.
findings.fix: Delete claim 10 and renumber. In 07 ¶15 delete the second and third sentences and keep only "The second side 16 of the base 12 forms the upper boundary of the chamber 22, and the chamber 22 is in fluid communication with the air-extraction mechanism 20." In ¶25 delete the sentence describing the duct as an upright hollow column. In ¶45 replace "withdraws air from the chamber 22 through the extraction opening 30 at a volumetric extraction rate" with "withdraws air from the chamber 22 at a volumetric extraction rate". Remove numerals 30 and 32 from draft/numerals.md. Remove 30 from figures/FIG-2 (delete the channel) and figures/FIG-3 (delete the circle and the sentence identifying it), remove 32 from figures/FIG-1 (delete the column and mount the pump housing directly on the slab), and amend 06-drawings FIG. 3 to "...showing the second side of the base and the perimeter member."

findings.title: Fasteners 54 and direct fastened motor mounting are untraced
findings.where: draft/08-claims.md claim 11; draft/07-detailed-description.md ¶19, ¶63; draft/numerals.md entry 54; figures/FIG-1 brief
findings.detail: The candidate recites the motor mounted directly against the first side and fixed by fasteners spaced around its foot, and draws two bolt-head blocks. findings.title: Exhaust outlet discharging to atmosphere is untraced
findings.detail: The candidate recites where the withdrawn air goes and a structural exhaust outlet on the pump housing. The disclosure says the mechanism removes air from the chamber and says nothing about discharge, an outlet, or its location. No affirmative USER passage describes an exhaust. The corrective turn lists 'exhaust to atmosphere' as already found unsupported.
findings.evidence: Candidate (07 ¶25): "withdraws air from the chamber 22 through the duct 32 and the extraction opening 30, discharging it to atmosphere through an exhaust outlet on the pump housing." Claim 9: "wherein the air-extraction mechanism is a vacuum pump carried on the base and having an exhaust outlet discharging to atmosphere." findings.fix: Amend claim 9 to read "9. The vibration device of claim 1, wherein the air-extraction mechanism is a vacuum pump." In 07 ¶25 replace the first sentence with "The air-extraction mechanism 20 is coupled to the first side 14 of the base 12 and withdraws air from the chamber 22."

findings.title: No-valve limitation and the vacuum-cannot-be-held reasoning are untraced
findings.detail: The candidate adds a negative structural limitation — the chamber is devoid of a valve operable to close it to atmosphere — and the accompanying reasoning. The disclosure never mentions a valve, in either the positive or the negative. Continuous operation is disclosed; the absence of a valve is a separate structural fact the inventor did not state. The corrective turn lists 'a no-valve limitation' as already found unsupported.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 7): "wherein the chamber is devoid of a valve operable to close the chamber to atmosphere, such that the pressure differential exists only while the air-extraction mechanism withdraws air from the chamber". (07 ¶27): "the chamber 22 is devoid of a valve operable to close the chamber 22 to atmosphere, and there is nothing in which a vacuum could be held." Nearest source (disclosure ¶13): "The air-extraction mechanism continuously removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter" — continuity of operation, not absence of a valve.
findings.fix: Amend claim 7 to read "7. The vibration device of claim 1, wherein the air-extraction mechanism is operable to withdraw air from the chamber continuously while the vibration motor operates." In 07 ¶27 delete "the chamber 22 is devoid of a valve operable to close the chamber 22 to atmosphere, and there is nothing in which a vacuum could be held. As explained below," so the paragraph reads "...It is not run to establish a vacuum and then stopped: the chamber 22 is never sealed, so the pressure differential exists only while the air-extraction mechanism 20 withdraws air from the chamber 22."

findings.title: Electrical supply 50, mains cord and battery alternative are untraced
findings.detail: The candidate adds a power source, its form as a flexible cord leaving the pump housing, a mains or site supply, a battery alternative carried on the base, and independent or common switching. The disclosure names no power source, no cord, no battery and no switch. No affirmative USER passage describes any of these; the drafting agent's own turn records 'power source' as a point where the disclosure gives no fact, and the corrective turn lists 'electrical cord or battery alternatives' as already found unsupported.
findings.evidence: Candidate (07 ¶29): "An electrical supply 50 provides power to the vibration motor 18 and... In the embodiment of FIG. 1 the electrical supply 50 is a flexible cord leaving the air-extraction mechanism 20 and running to a mains or site supply; a battery carried on the base 12 may be used instead. The vibration motor 18 and the air-extraction mechanism 20 may be switched together or independently of one another." Nearest source (disclosure ¶11): the disclosure recites only "a vibration motor" and "An air-extraction mechanism, such as a vacuum pump" with no power supply of any kind.
findings.fix: Delete 07 ¶29 in full. Delete numeral 50 from draft/numerals.md. Delete the electrical supply bullet and numeral 50 from figures/FIG-1 and replace "Every body except the cord has flat faces and straight edges" in its View line with "Every body has flat faces and straight edges."

findings.title: Integral one-piece perimeter member and fastened perimeter joint are untraced
findings.detail: The candidate recites two alternative constructions for joining the perimeter member to the base — fasteners, or integral formation as one piece — neither of which the inventor stated. The disclosure describes the perimeter of the second side as being formed as a rigid loop or skirt but specifies no joint, no fasteners and no one-piece construction. Claim 12: "wherein the perimeter member is formed integrally with the base as one piece." Nearest source (disclosure ¶11): "The perimeter of the second side is formed as a rigid loop or skirt made from a low-friction material..."

findings.title: Attachment formation 48, its low placement, and plural attachment formations are untraced
findings.where: draft/08-claims.md claims 14 and 19; draft/07-detailed-description.md ¶79, ¶81, ¶83; draft/numerals.md entry 48; figures/FIG-5 brief
findings.detail: The candidate adds a named attachment formation on the base, places it low and close to the plane of the bearing face, derives a moment-limiting benefit from that placement, offers one at each end of the base, and draws it as a large eye. The disclosure says only that the flexible element is connected to the device; it says nothing about where or how.
